findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature :: Rotating the signing secret, with the client secret left blank, is saved at once; crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/instance_integration_setup.rs:1429 then_on_instance_page
findings.obligation: D16: the notice a stored Slack change earned (I-10 here) waits as a one-shot value under one session key in the admin's own session and is taken out as the page reads it, so the notice is never a query value - an address alone, typed again, bookmarked or shared, carries neither a submitted value nor a notice and claims no change that was not made.
findings.observation: The negative arm of D16 has no falsifier anywhere, so the mechanism D16 forbids passes every case. then_on_instance_page (support:1429-1438) asserts answer.path.split('?').next() == Some(INSTANCE_INTEGRATIONS), which a '?saved=...' landing address satisfies; no scenario in the feature file opens the landed address a second time (grep for reload, bookmark, typed again, query, notice returns only unrelated comment lines); and SavedNotice::left_waiting and taken_from (crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/handlers/instance.rs:423 and :432) have no test in crates/foundry-app/src (grep: two hits, the definition and its one call site). A Foundry that carried the notice back as a query value, or that left the notice in the session so a later plain GET of /admin/instance/integrations also reads 'Saved. Workspace admins can now choose Add to Slack.', passes all 29 cases of the us-iis-05 lane and all nine S1 rows. The positive arm is observed; only the claim that an address alone claims nothing is unobserved.
findings.remediation: Add the two cheap public-port readings D16 already names to S1's rotation scenario, or as one further S1 row: after the save, the address Priya landed on carries no query, and a second plain GET of /admin/instance/integrations by the same admin reads the page without 'Saved. Workspace admins can now choose Add to Slack.' (support already has then_reads_nothing_saying and instance_page for exactly this reading). If instead D16's negative arm is meant as internal mechanism rather than a promised outcome, design records it as a decision it does not promise to observe, so the oracle is not expected to carry it. This is a completion obligation of the feature, not a craft prerequisite: S1's craft has shipped and the rows S1 was approved for are intact.

The single S1 acceptance-row delta, judged sound. Diffing acceptance.md's '### S1' section between fcf3022 and HEAD returns exactly one changed line: the P2 field-shape row's Tested locator moved from the descriptive 'crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/slack_app.rs :: the field-shape table and the generated field cases of the decision module' to the concrete test name 'crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/slack_app.rs :: a_value_is_judged_the_same_with_surrounding_whitespace' (bound at 2f9d415, the S3 oracle commit). The row's expected text claims three verdicts. The named property observes the first (slack_app.rs:615-622: for any_field() and any value of 0-40 characters, field.check(whitespace + value + whitespace) equals field.check(value)). The other two are observed by named sibling properties in the same module, which the S3 rows now bind by name: any_32_lowercase_hex_is_accepted_as_a_secret (slack_app.rs:626, acceptance.md line 1039) and a_character_outside_the_alphabet_is_refused_as_malformed (slack_app.rs:635, acceptance.md line 1068), with a_save_is_refused_on_the_first_blank_or_malformed_field_in_form_order (slack_app.rs:565, line 1097) covering form order. The executable set therefore did not shrink; one locator was narrowed and is duplicated at acceptance.md line 1010, and the obligation-to-observation relation still closes over the record. Not a defect.

The design amendment at 371398e, measured against S1's oracle: D18's S1 arm is observed, D16's negative arm is not. D18 (the I-14 gate decided inside the write's own locked transaction, Store::store_slack_submission): its zero-count arm is S1's own row - feature:781 'Another Slack app entered with both secrets takes over at once while no workspace is connected' posts the real door and then observes Add to Slack asking Slack's approval for the new client ID, so a gate that held the submission with nobody connected fails there; the nonzero arm and the connect-in-flight race are S2's rows and the foundry-store tests, not S1's promises. Moving the decision from the handler into the store is invisible at the public port, which is why the lane is green at byte-identical oracle bytes; no S1 observation was weakened. D16 (post, redirect, get, with the notice a one-shot value in the admin's own session): its positive arm is observed - every S1 save reads 'Saved. Workspace admins can now choose Add to Slack.' and then 'Priya is on the instance integrations page'. Its negative arm, stated in the same decision - the notice is never a query value, and an address alone, typed again, bookmarked or shared, carries neither a submitted value nor a notice and claims no change that was not made - has no falsifier: then_on_instance_page (support:1429-1438) compares answer.path.split('?').next() with INSTANCE_INTEGRATIONS, so the '?saved=' address D16 forbids satisfies it; grep of the feature file for reload, bookmark, typed again, query and notice returns no scenario that opens the landed address a second time; and SavedNotice::left_waiting and taken_from (handlers/instance.rs:423 and :432) have no test anywhere in crates/foundry-app/src (argv 'grep -rn "taken_from\|left_waiting" crates/foundry-app/src/' exit 0, two hits: the definition and its one call site). Recorded as the finding of this round.

diagnostic: Accepted: the S1 oracle at 371398e still reads the observations it was approved for, and no shared step was weakened. S1's nine row-bearing scenarios are byte-identical to the approved revision fcf3022, tags and all (the feature-file delta is exactly two hunks: the head scope note, and a pure append after the last S1 scenario). Every support and step change made by S2 and S3 is additive: the only deleted lines are four step regexes and two match arms, each widened by alternation with its body and support call unchanged, and all six support hunks insert between items. Of the 27 support functions S1's bound steps call, every body is byte-identical (23 in instance_integration_setup.rs, 4 in external_integration_plugins.rs, a file unchanged since fcf3022), and all 78 expanded S1 step lines full-match exactly one of the 2994 step definitions at HEAD - the same definition function as at fcf3022, so none of the 19 added definitions shadows an S1 step. The one S1 acceptance-row delta is sound: the P2 field-shape row's locator was narrowed from a descriptive phrase to the concrete property a_value_is_judged_the_same_with_surrounding_whitespace, while the row's two other verdicts are bound by name in the S3 rows to sibling properties in the same module, so the executable set did not shrink. Runner evidence is reused against a byte comparison, not restamped: the us-iis-05 lane (28 tagged scenarios, 29 executed cases, all nine S1 scenarios among them) and the full instance-integration-setup lane are exit 0 in runs/craft.S3.json at e941b18, and 'git diff --name-only e941b18 371398e -- crates/' is empty, so oracle, supports, production and runtime are identical to that run; no lane was run in this round. D18's S1 arm is observed by the takeover row at feature:781 and its move into the locked store write is invisible at the public port. One non-blocking finding, owner oracle: D16's negative arm - an address alone carries no notice and claims no change - has no falsifier, because then_on_instance_page strips the query before comparing, no scenario opens the landed address twice, and SavedNotice::left_waiting/taken_from are untested; a query-carried or sticky notice passes all 29 cases.
